sample.title: Learning objective
sample.body: By the end of the period, students can move a term across the equals sign by changing its sign (+ becomes −, × becomes ÷), and check the answer by substitution.

sample.title: Prerequisite check
sample.body: Two quick questions, answered on fingers or in rough work. If many get Q1 wrong, spend one minute on adding and subtracting negative numbers first.

sample.title: Hook
sample.body: Draw a balance (taraazu) on the board with 3x + 5 on one pan and 20 on the other. Ask: "If I take 5 away from the left pan, what must I do to the right pan to keep it level?" Take two or three answers before moving on.

sample.title: Explanation — #1
sample.body: 21 students moved a term across "=" without changing its sign — for example "3x = 20 + 5" (Periodic Test 1, Q7). Show why it is wrong: subtract 5 from BOTH sides — 3x + 5 − 5 = 20 − 5 — so 3x = 20 − 5. "Transposing" is only a shortcut for doing the same thing to both sides; the sign flips because we subtracted. Write the rule: + ↔ −, × ↔ ÷ when a term crosses "=".

sample.title: Worked example
sample.body: Solve 4x + 5 = 2x + 13 together. Step 1: 4x − 2x = 13 − 5. Step 2: 2x = 8. Step 3: x = 4. Check: 4(4) + 5 = 21, 2(4) + 13 = 21 ✓. Ask a student to say each sign change aloud as you write it.

sample.title: Tackle a misconception — #2
sample.body: 8 students applied an operation to one side only, e.g. "3x + 5 − 5 = 20 → 3x = 20" (Periodic Test 1, Q7). Put it on the board without saying whose it is and ask: "Is the balance still level?" Then fix it together: whatever you do to the left, do to the right. (4 more had the right method but slipped on arithmetic — remind everyone to check by substituting.)

sample.title: Guided practice
sample.body: In the peer pairs below, solve: (a) x + 9 = 4, (b) 3y − 7 = 11, (c) 12 − 2p = 4. The mentor explains each sign change; the learner writes. Walk round and check line 1 of every answer — that is where the sign error shows up.

sample.title: Exit ticket
sample.body: Students attempt the 4 exit-ticket questions alone on a half sheet with name and roll number. Collect them, photograph them and upload them to RedPen for grading.

sample.title: Board plan
sample.body:
LHS | RHS
3x + 5 = 20
3x + 5 − 5 = 20 − 5   (same on both sides)
3x = 15
x = 5
Shortcut: +5 crosses "=" → becomes −5
Rule: + ↔ −    × ↔ ÷
Check: 3(5) + 5 = 20 ✓

sample.title: Peer pairs
sample.body: Each mentor scored at least 60% on this concept; learners scored under 50%. Mentors explain, learners write. Reshuffle if two friends will chat.

sample.title: Extension work
sample.body: For students who finish early: (1) Solve (x/3) + 4 = 10. (2) Make up an equation whose answer is x = −2 and swap it with a partner. (3) In one sentence, explain why −2y = 1 − 7 and not 1 + 7.
